title: Neutral outflows in high-z QSOs
question: To detect outflowing neutral gas in five strongly lensed z~2-4 QSOs using OH+(1_1-1_0), CO(9-8), and underlying dust continuum observations, and compare their outflow and warm molecular gas properties to high-z star-forming and active galaxies.

data.sensitivity: 0.071 to 0.40 mJy beam^-1 per 100 km s^-1

what.value: 500 um continuum flux densities, FIR luminosities (40-120 um), dust temperatures, and redshifts for MG J0414+0534 and PSS J2322+1944 from Herschel/SPIRE follow-up of gravitationally lensed QSOs

evidence.quote: The five quasars were selected based on their 500 $\mu$m continuum flux densities from a sample of 104 gravitationally lensed QSOs presented in (cite: Stacey2018).

The sources are listed in both the CASTLES survey (cite: Kochanek1999) and Sloan Digital Sky Survey Quasar Lens Search catalogue (cite: Inada2012), which have since been followed up with *Herschel*/SPIRE observations (cite: Stacey2018), providing accurate estimates of their FIR-luminosities and dust temperatures (Table [\[tab:derived\]](#tab:derived)).

what.value: Comparison sample of high-z sources with OH+ and CO(9-8) measurements: obscured QSO W0410-0913, unobscured QSO SDSS J231038.88+185519.7, and DSFGs (HerBS-89a and Riechers et al. 2021b sample)

evidence.quote: We compared our results with high-z sources from the literature with comparable FIR luminosities, including obscured (W0410$-$0913 $z$=3.592 (cite: Stanley2021)) and unobscured (SDSS J231038.88+185519.7 $z$=6.0031, (cite: Shao2022)) QSOs, and DSFGs (HerBS-89a $z$=2.95 (cite: Berta2021) and the sample of (cite: Riechers2021b)).

what.value: Low-z L'_CO(9-8)-L_FIR correlation and Class I, II, III galaxy comparison data

evidence.quote: Our sample of high-z QSOs follow the $\rm L^\prime_{CO(9-8)}$–$\rm L_{FIR}$ correlation found in low–z galaxies (cite: Liu2015), with MG J0414+0534 falling the farthest from the relation towards lower $\rm L^\prime_{\rm CO(9-8)}/L_{\rm FIR}$ ratios (Fig. [2](#fig:derived)c).

At low–$z$, sources categorised into Class I, II, and III in order of increasing CO excitation, showed trends of falling above, on, and both above and below the relation with greater scatter, respectively ((cite: Rosenberg2015), Fig.[2](#fig:derived)).

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA visibility data into sideband spectral cubes
recipe.method: Reduce raw data in CASA and non-interactively image with tclean without continuum subtraction, separating the two sidebands into two cubes at native channel resolution
key_parameters: robust = 0.5, noise threshold = 1 sigma, frequency resolution = 15.624 MHz

recipe.goal: Extract spatially integrated spectra and fit spectral lines and continuum
recipe.method: Iterative two-pass spatial integration and simultaneous multi-Gaussian + linear continuum fitting: first sum spaxels with continuum >= 3 sigma from initial line-free channels, fit spectral components, then include any spaxel with channel value >= 3 sigma within the FWHM of CO(9-8) components and refit
key_parameters: Spaxel selection threshold >= 3 sigma (continuum in pass 1, CO(9-8) FWHM channel peak in pass 2)
assumptions: Same line parameters used to describe the OH+(1_1-1_0) and OH+(2_1-1_0) transitions; CO(9-8) central velocity used as systemic velocity for Doppler shifts

recipe.goal: Derive integrated optical depths, column densities, and line luminosities
recipe.method: Compute integrated OH+ absorption optical depths from transmitted and continuum flux, and compute OH+ and CO(9-8) line luminosities using Solomon et al. (1992) expressions
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with Omega_m = 0.307 and H_0 = 67.7 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; luminosities not corrected for lensing magnification

score_reason: Single ALMA project code (2019.1.01802.S) is clearly identified, imaging parameters (robust=0.5, 1-sigma threshold, native 15.624 MHz channels, no continuum subtraction) and the two-step 3-sigma spaxel integration + curve_fit multi-Gaussian fitting recipe are well described, and comprehensive numeric tables of fitted and derived quantities are provided. Minor deductions for missing tclean pixel size, OH+ column density conversion formula, and initial guesses/bounds for degenerate multi-Gaussian fits.
rediscovery_reason: Public single-project ALMA dataset (2019.1.01802.S) on 5 bright lensed QSOs with a straightforward imaging and 1D spectral extraction/fitting workflow and complete numeric answer keys for continuum fluxes, line fluxes, velocities, dispersions, optical depths, and luminosities.
